subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Biomimicry: Engineering Inspired by Nature
description: Learn Biomimicry: Engineering Inspired by Nature in one minute.

hook.text: Velcro was invented after a Swiss engineer noticed burrs on his dog's fur. Nature's hook-and-loop became a billion-dollar product.

buildup.text: Biomimicry copies designs refined over millions of years. Shark skin, lotus leaves, and gecko feet all inspire technology.

discovery.text: Shark skin has tiny tooth-like scales that reduce drag. Speedo's Fastskin copied the pattern — banned for being too effective.

twist.text: The Shinkansen had a noise problem. A birdwatcher engineer redesigned the nose to mimic a kingfisher's beak — and it worked.

climax.text: Termite mounds maintain constant temperature without AC. The Eastgate Centre in Zimbabwe copied their ventilation design.

punchline.text: 3.8 billion years of R&D. Free to copy. Nature is the original engineer.

quiz.question: How did biomimicry solve the Shinkansen bullet train's noise problem?
options: Sound-absorbing panels modeled after owl feathers were added to the exterior
An engineer redesigned the nose to mimic a kingfisher's beak for quieter air entry
The train's wheels were coated with a rubber compound inspired by cat paw pads
